export const meta = {
  name: 'phase2-translator-build',
  description: 'Build the pkp-to-ControlScript translator test-first, with a wire-table oracle and validation across all four sample pairs',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Oracle', detail: 'build tools/wire_table.py — the acceptance harness' },
    { title: 'Translate', detail: 'build tools/pkp2cs.py — the AST transformer' },
    { title: 'Validate', detail: 'run across all four device pairs and report residuals' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'adversarial code review of both tools' },
  ],
}

const R = '/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert'

const GROUND = `
PROJECT: ${R}. Building the Extron .pkp -> ControlScript .py translator.

ESTABLISHED (trust; findings/02 and findings/06 have the detail):
- A .pkp is gzip over a .NET BinaryFormatter (NRBF) stream. Parser exists:
  'python3 ${R}/tools/pkp_dump.py <file.pkp> -o out.json'. It emits a flat objects table with
  $ref edges; --resolve inlines them (memoized).
- The .pkp EMBEDS one Python driver per transport as StreamResourceAsset byte arrays, written
  against the Global Configurator runtime (Extron2.BaseDriver, or Extron2.HTTPDriver for REST
  devices). The shipped ControlScript module is a different Python dialect over 'extronlib'.
- The convertible region of the embedded script is delimited by literal markers:
  '### BEGIN AUTO GENERATION OF COMMAND DEF' ... '### END'. It is 72-78% of each file.
- Multi-transport packages appear as N_models x N_transports DriverModelAssets, each owning ONE
  ProtocolAsset child (SerialProtocolAsset / EthernetProtocolAsset) plus its own
  _scriptFileName and _scriptClassName.
- Metadata that matters: EnumStateAsset._tag holds wire tokens (e.g. 'Audio' -> '$');
  DecimalParamAsset carries _min/_max/_suffix; DriverModelAsset._name is the model name;
  per-model command registries are the correctly PRUNED command inventory (the file-level master
  list contains orphans reachable from no model).

THE REWRITE RULES already derived from comparing embedded scripts to shipped modules:
- '_cmd_Set<X>' / '_cmd_Update<X>'  ->  'Set<X>' / 'Update<X>'
- 'self.Write<X>(value, qualifier, \\'Live\\')'  ->  'self.WriteStatus(\\'<X>\\', value, qualifier)'
- the per-command 'Write<X>' / 'Read<X>' wrapper defs are DELETED (the target defines only
  WriteStatus / ReadStatus once)
- the 'if self.__SafeToSet(\\'X\\'):' guard is unwrapped, and the preceding 'Emulated' pre-write
  is deleted
- 'self.DriverCmd(\\'UpdateAllMatrixTie\\', None, None)'  ->  direct call
  'self.UpdateAllMatrixTie(None, None)'
- match-string handlers keep their '(self, match, tag)' signature
- command methods are emitted ALPHABETICALLY by command name, even where the Commands dict is not
  alphabetical
- the Commands dict drops the Set/Update/Live/Emulated booleans, keeping only Parameters and Status
- 'ConnectionStatus': {'Status': {}} is PREPENDED (it is not a device command; the template writes
  it from OnConnected/OnDisconnected)
- 'isinstance(self, <scriptClassName>)'  ->  'self.ModelName == <DriverModelAsset._name>'
- self.Models is generated from the DriverModelAsset names
- the runtime shell (DeviceClass.__init__ boilerplate, __SetHelper/__UpdateHelper, everything from
  the 'RECOMMENDED not to modify' banner to EOF, and the transport mixin classes) is a fixed
  TEMPLATE that is copied, not derived. The last ~170 lines of two shipped modules are identical
  except whitespace.

DROPPED WITH NO TARGET (must be reported, never silently discarded):
- the GC dual-status model: WriteStatusHelper/ReadStatusHelper with Mutex(), ExtronTime timestamps,
  PostNewStatusEx, _cmd_SetSyncEmulatedStatus, StatusRefresh, and 'class ExtronTime(float)'.
- any 'Read<X>(..., \\'Emulated\\')' whose target is a GC-only scratch command.
- hand-written code outside the BEGIN/END markers.

THE FOUR ORACLE PAIRS (each: a .pkp and the shipped ControlScript module for the same device):
1. DSC 12G-HD    — SIS, ethernet/SSH, 1 model
   "${R}/samples/DSC_12G-HD/pkp/extr_17_17677_v1_0_0.pkp"
   "${R}/samples/DSC_12G-HD/controlscript/extr_scaler_DSC_12G_HD_A_v1_0_0_0.py"
2. DTP3 CP 42    — SIS, ethernet/SSH, matrix, 2 models (incl. a USB subclass)
   "${R}/samples/DTP3 CP 42/pkp/extr_15_17578_v1_3_0.pkp"
   "${R}/samples/DTP3 CP 42/controlscript/extr_matrix_DTP3_CrossPoint_42_Series_v1_2_0_0.py"
3. Samsung QN43LS03DAFXZA — NON-SIS, binary serial with checksum, 12 DriverModelAssets
   "${R}/samples/Samsung QNxxLS03DAFXZA/pkp/smsg_10_6738_v1_0_0.pkp"
   "${R}/samples/Samsung QNxxLS03DAFXZA/controlscript/smsg_display_QNxxLS03DAFXZA_Series_v1_0_0_0.py"
4. Automate VX   — NON-SIS, HTTP/REST + JSON, Extron2.HTTPDriver
   "${R}/samples/Automate VX/pkp/1bynd_42_4279_v1_0_11.pkp"
   "${R}/samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py"

CRITICAL ACCEPTANCE PRINCIPLE — this is the project's standing lesson:
Do NOT measure success by textual or line similarity to the shipped module. Line overlap between
a package's embedded script and its shipped module varies from 76% (DSC) to 38% (Samsung) while
the command tables stay nearly identical, because shipped modules carry version skew, hand-edits
and dropped throttles. SUCCESS IS MEASURED ON THE WIRE-STRING TABLE: for each command, the
command-string template, the response regex, the value maps and the parameter list must match.

Known expected residuals (these are Extron's own inconsistencies, NOT translator bugs):
- DSC: UpdateLogoAssignment differs by a hand-edit; the .pkp version never references the Logo
  qualifier and is the more broken of the two. Match string 'E(\\d+)' vs 'E(\\d{2})'. A
  LogoAvailability throttle present in the .pkp is dropped in the shipped module.
- DTP3: the shipped module is v1.2.0.0 while the package is v1.3.0 — real version skew, including
  three USB commands. 'MatrixIONumberSelect' is an orphan. Five bugged commands sit only in the
  file-level master list, not under any model.
- Samsung: the shipped module derives from the SERIAL embedded script only; Extron ships no
  IP-path module for this device at all.

RULES:
- WORK TEST-FIRST. Write the test, watch it FAIL, then make it pass. Report actual command output,
  never a claim that tests pass.
- pytest is NOT installed. Use a plain 'python3 test_x.py' runner with asserts, matching the style
  of the existing ${R}/tools/test_pkg_dump.py.
- Python 3 standard library only. No new dependencies.
- FAIL LOUDLY. Never emit a driver that silently omits something. Anything not translated must be
  reported in a structured 'residuals' list with a reason.
- Cite real command output in your report. Do not paraphrase test results.
`

phase('Oracle')
log('Phase 2 stage 1: building the wire-table oracle')

const oracle = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nYOUR TASK: build ${R}/tools/wire_table.py — the ACCEPTANCE ORACLE that makes the
whole project measurable. Nothing else can be validated until this exists, so it matters more than
it looks.

It must extract, from a Python driver file, a normalised table of what that driver puts on the wire:

  for each command: name, parameter list, the command-string template(s) it builds,
                    the response pattern(s) it matches, and any value maps
                    (e.g. {'Fill': '1', 'Follow': '2'})

It must work on BOTH dialects — a shipped ControlScript module (class DeviceClass, self.Commands,
AddMatchString, Set*/Update* methods) and a GC embedded script (Extron2.BaseDriver or
Extron2.HTTPDriver, _cmd_Set*/_cmd_Update*, the same AddMatchString idiom) — and normalise them to
the SAME shape so the two can be diffed directly.

Use the 'ast' module, not regex, to find: the Commands dict literal, AddMatchString calls, the
per-command method bodies, and string-building expressions. Command strings are often built by
.format(), f-strings, %-formatting, str concatenation, struct.pack, or a helper like self.build();
normalise these to a canonical template representation (e.g. 'w1*{}ASPR\\r' with a marked
substitution slot, or for binary protocols a byte-sequence template with slots). Where a value is
not statically resolvable, record it as an opaque marker rather than guessing — and count how often
that happens, since that number bounds the oracle's usefulness.

Also provide a 'diff' entrypoint that takes two tables and reports: commands only in A, only in B,
and for shared commands any difference in template, regex, value map or parameter list.

Test-first against all four oracle pairs. The tests should assert specific known facts — for
example that the DSC table contains AspectRatio with template 'w1*{}ASPR\\r' and value map
{'Fill': '1', 'Follow': '2'}, and that the Samsung table contains SetVolume building
08 22 01 00 00 <vol> with a twos-complement checksum. Extract the embedded scripts from the .pkp
files with pkp_dump.py as part of your fixture setup.

Report: what you built, the ACTUAL test output, the per-pair extraction statistics (commands found,
templates resolved, opaque markers), and an honest statement of what the oracle cannot see.`,
  { label: 'build:wire_table', phase: 'Oracle', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
)

phase('Translate')
log('Phase 2 stage 2: building the translator')

const translator = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nThe acceptance oracle now exists at ${R}/tools/wire_table.py. Here is the report
from the agent that built it:\n\n${oracle}\n\n---\n\nYOUR TASK: build ${R}/tools/pkp2cs.py — the
.pkp -> ControlScript translator. Work test-first; write ${R}/tools/test_pkp2cs.py.

Pipeline:
 1. EXTRACT — use pkp_dump.py as a library (import it; do not shell out) to parse the .pkp, pull
    every StreamResourceAsset script, and read the DriverModelAsset tree. Detect multi-transport
    packages by grouping DriverModelAssets on the class of their single ProtocolAsset child. Emit
    one translation job per transport.
 2. ANALYSE — parse the embedded script with 'ast'. Locate the class deriving from BaseDriver or
    HTTPDriver, the self.Commands dict literal, the AddMatchString calls, the BEGIN/END marker
    region, and the per-command method groups keyed by their <X> suffix.
 3. TRANSFORM — apply the rewrite rules from the brief. Do this on the AST or on a
    marker-delimited source region with precise edits; do NOT do blind regex over the whole file.
 4. EMIT — splice the transformed command block into the fixed DeviceClass/transport-mixin
    template, generate self.Models from the DriverModelAsset names, and carry through
    device-specific __init__ state.
 5. REPORT — return a structured result: the generated module, plus a 'residuals' list naming
    everything dropped or flagged (GC dual-status constructs, Emulated reads of scratch commands,
    code outside the markers, unresolved constructs) with a reason for each.

The template: derive it from the shipped modules, which are identical except whitespace from the
'RECOMMENDED not to modify' banner to EOF. Do not invent it. Parameterise only what genuinely
varies (class names, model map, transport mixins present).

TRANSPORT COVERAGE: the four pairs span SSH/ethernet, binary serial, and HTTP/REST. The samples do
not show every transport mixin ControlScript supports. Where you cannot derive a mixin from
evidence, do not guess — emit only the mixins the evidence supports and record the limitation.

VALIDATION IS THE POINT. For each of the four pairs: translate the .pkp, run wire_table.py over
both your output and the shipped module, and diff. Iterate until the only differences are the
KNOWN EXPECTED RESIDUALS listed in the brief. Do not chase textual similarity.

Report: what you built, ACTUAL test output, and a per-pair table of wire-table diffs with each
remaining difference classified as expected-residual or genuine-gap.`,
  { label: 'build:pkp2cs', phase: 'Translate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
)

phase('Validate')
log('Phase 2 stage 3: independent validation across all four pairs')

const validation = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nThe oracle (${R}/tools/wire_table.py) and translator (${R}/tools/pkp2cs.py) now
exist. Build reports:\n\nORACLE:\n${oracle}\n\nTRANSLATOR:\n${translator}\n\n---\n\nYOUR TASK:
INDEPENDENTLY validate. Do not trust either report — run everything yourself.

For each of the four device pairs:
 1. Run the translator on the .pkp.
 2. Run wire_table.py over the generated module and over the shipped module.
 3. Diff, and classify EVERY difference as: expected-residual (matching the known list in the
    brief), genuine translator gap, or oracle blind spot.
 4. Verify the generated module at least PARSES ('python3 -m py_compile') and that its class
    structure matches the shipped module's shape.

Then stress the honesty of the tooling:
 - Does the translator's residuals list actually name everything it dropped? Pick a construct you
   know is dropped (the GC dual-status helpers, ExtronTime, an Emulated scratch read) and confirm
   it appears in residuals rather than vanishing silently.
 - Feed it something malformed — a truncated .pkp, a script with no BEGIN/END markers — and confirm
   it fails loudly rather than emitting a plausible-looking but wrong module.

Produce a scorecard: per pair, commands in the shipped module, commands generated, wire-templates
matching, regexes matching, value maps matching, and the residual list. Give an overall honest
assessment of how close this is to usable, and name the single biggest weakness.

You may FIX small bugs you find in either tool, but say exactly what you changed and re-run the
tests afterwards. Do not restructure either tool.`,
  { label: 'validate:four-pairs', phase: 'Validate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
)

phase('Review')
const review = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nYOU ARE AN ADVERSARIAL CODE REVIEWER. Read ${R}/tools/wire_table.py,
${R}/tools/pkp2cs.py and their test files as they stand on disk. Ignore what the build reports
claim — read the code.

Validation report for context:\n${validation}\n\nFind:
 - Correctness bugs: AST handling that breaks on constructs present in the four samples, rewrite
   rules applied too broadly or too narrowly, string-building normalisation that would produce a
   WRONG wire template (the worst failure mode here — a driver that looks right and sends the wrong
   bytes).
 - Silent failures: any path that swallows an exception, returns partial data, or emits a module
   without recording what it dropped. The brief demanded fail-loud; verify it.
 - Tests that assert nothing meaningful, or that would pass against a broken implementation.
 - Over-fitting: rules that work only because of a coincidence in these four samples and would
   break on a fifth device.

Report findings ranked by severity, each with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. Do NOT fix
anything — report only. Be specific and skeptical; a plausible-looking translator that emits subtly
wrong wire strings is worse than no translator.`,
  { label: 'review:adversarial', phase: 'Review', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
)

return { oracle, translator, validation, review }

result.oracle:
## Summary

Built `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/wire_table.py` — the wire-string acceptance oracle — plus `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/test_wire_table.py`.

**How it works:** `extract_table(source)` parses a driver file with `ast`, finds the main `class`, the `self.Commands = {...}` dict (for names/parameters), every `AddMatchString(re.compile(pattern), handler, tag)` call, and every `Set*`/`Update*` (or `_cmd_Set*`/`_cmd_Update*`) method. For each command it walks the Set/Update method's statements (branch-aware — each `if`/`else` arm gets its own env, so `SetMatrixTieCommand`'s two branches produce two distinct templates) to find the `self.__SetHelper`/`self.__UpdateHelper` call, then symbolically resolves the command-string argument with a small `Resolver`: literals pass through; `dict[value]` lookups against a literal dict are captured as a named value-map and contribute a `{}` slot; `.format()`, string concatenation, f-strings, `struct.pack`/`self.<helper>()` byte-builders (inlined one level, e.g. Samsung's `self.build()`), and a two's-complement-checksum idiom (`~sum(...) & 0xFF`) are all recognized. Everything else becomes an `('opaque', source)` leaf that increments a counted `opaque_markers` stat rather than being guessed. It auto-detects the HTTP dialect (`__SetHelper(cmd, value, qualifier, url=..., data=...)`) vs the SIS dialect (`__SetHelper(cmd, cmdstring, value, qualifier)`) by argument shape, so the same extractor covers both `Extron2.BaseDriver`/ControlScript `SerialInterface` and `Extron2.HTTPDriver`/`HTTPClass`. `diff_tables(a, b)` reports commands only in A/B, and for shared commands, differences in parameters, templates, **slot sources** (catches same-shape-different-content residuals), responses, and value maps.

**Actual test output** (`python3 -W ignore tools/test_wire_table.py`): `34 passed, 0 failed, 34 total`, run against real fixtures extracted straight from the four `.pkp` files via `pkp_dump.PkpParser` (no hand-copied embedded scripts — `tools/out/embedded/` now also has Samsung serial+ethernet and Automate VX embedded scripts pulled the same way as the pre-existing DSC/DTP3 ones).

**Per-pair extraction statistics** (from the test run, `stats` dict per table):
- DSC shipped: 29 commands, 19 Set + 24 Update templates resolved, 30 AddMatchString (27 mapped to commands, 3 unmapped — e.g. `Error`, `Verbose`/`Echo` mode handlers with no `Set`/`Update`), **0 opaque markers**. DSC embedded: 30 commands, 20+24 templates, **1 opaque** (`UserDefinedCommand`'s raw pass-through `cmdstring.encode`).
- DTP3 shipped: 31 commands, 18+16 templates, 29 match strings (22 mapped, 7 unmapped — status-only handlers like `__MatchAllTie`/`__MatchIndividualTie` with no 1:1 command), **1 opaque** (`MatrixIONameCommand`'s raw string).
- Samsung shipped: 9 commands, 8+4 templates, 4/4 match strings mapped, **0 opaque** after fixing the resolver (see below). Samsung embedded (serial): 10 commands, 9+4 templates, **1 opaque**.
- Automate VX shipped: 18 commands, 17+8 templates, 0 match strings (confirmed HTTP dialect has none), **4 opaque** (`PanTilt`/`Zoom` in both Set methods — see limitation below). Embedded: 17 commands, same shape, 4 opaque.

**Bugs found and fixed while getting real fixtures to resolve correctly** (all caught by watching tests fail first):
1. Name resolution order: a helper method's own formal parameter (e.g. Samsung's `def build(self, cmd1, cmd2, cmd3, value)`) coincidentally named the same as the caller's parameter (`value`) was resolving to the wrong binding, and in one case recursed to `<max-depth>`. Fixed by resolving call arguments eagerly against the *caller's* scope before substituting them into the callee's, storing already-resolved values rather than raw AST nodes.
2. `AddMatchString`/helper calls appearing inside an `if` **test** expression (e.g. `if self.__UpdateHelper(...):`) were invisible to the branch walker, which only scanned `.body`/`.orelse`.
3. Added a value-map projection for `ValueStateValues[value][0]`-style double subscripts (multi-byte Samsung commands whose map values are tuples) rather than giving up.
4. Added a `slots` field alongside `canonical` template strings specifically to catch the DSC `UpdateLogoAssignment` residual (findings/06): both dialects render the identical shape `'wA{}LOGO\r'`, but the `.pkp` version feeds the slot from the bare `value` parameter while the shipped module correctly uses `qualifier['Logo']` — a same-shape, different-wire-content bug that canonical-string diffing alone would have missed. This is exactly the kind of thing `diff_tables` now surfaces (`test_dsc_diff_shipped_vs_embedded_surfaces_known_logo_assignment_residual`), along with the documented `E(\d+)` vs `E(\d{2})` Error-regex residual (`test_dsc_diff_shipped_vs_embedded_error_regex_residual`).

**What the oracle honestly cannot see** (counted, not silently dropped):
- Runtime-composed strings with no static template at all (`UserDefinedCommand`/`MatrixIONameCommand`: literally `value.encode()` passed straight to the wire) — correctly reported opaque; there is no template to recover.
- A value assigned differently in two sibling `if`/`else` branches but consumed by a **single** helper call *after* the branch (Automate VX's `SetPanTilt`/`SetZoom`, which build `PanTiltCmdString`/`data` differently per branch, then call `self.__SetHelper` once afterward) — since the extractor snapshots one env per call site rather than forking on branch-local rebindings, this reports `OPAQUE:PanTiltCmdString`/`OPAQUE:data` rather than resolving two variants. The idiomatic pattern where each branch calls the helper directly (DTP3's `SetMatrixTieCommand`) *is* fully resolved. This gap is bounded and visible in `opaque_markers` (4 in both Automate VX tables) rather than hidden.
- Templates fed purely by a dict-map lookup (`ValueStateValues[value]`) collapse to a bare `{}` in the canonical shape; the actual content lives only in `value_maps`, so a shape-only glance can't tell you the wire content — you have to read `value_map` too (by design, and tested explicitly).
- Only one level of `self.<method>()` inlining is attempted by default (depth-capped at 10) — deeply nested helper chains beyond that would fall back to opaque.

Files: `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/wire_table.py`, `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/test_wire_table.py`, and cached fixtures under `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/out/embedded/`.

## Summary

Built `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/pkp2cs.py` (1252 lines) — the `.pkp` → ControlScript translator — and `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/test_pkp2cs.py` (430 lines, plain `test_*`/assert style, no pytest).

**Pipeline implementation:**
- **EXTRACT** (`discover_jobs`): imports `pkp_dump` as a library, walks the raw NRBF object graph directly (no `--resolve`, to avoid the documented blow-up) via a small generic-wrapper-unwinding helper (`unwrap_generic_wrapper`/`child_collection_items`) that drills through the `AssetBase\`1[[I...Asset]]` indirection NRBF uses for every child slot. Groups `DriverModelAsset`s by `_scriptFileName` (one `TranslationJob` per embedded script/transport), and per model records `_scriptClassName`, display `_name`, and the concrete `ProtocolAsset` class. Verified against all four samples: DSC→1 job/1 model, DTP3→1 job/2 models, Samsung→2 jobs (serial×6 models, ethernet×6 models), Automate VX→1 job/3 models (all sharing one script class, confirmed by NRBF, not guessed).
- **ANALYSE/TRANSFORM** (`analyse`, `GenericBodyRewriter`): parses the embedded script with `ast`, extracts `self.Commands` via `ast.literal_eval`, collects `AddMatchString` calls, and applies one AST rewrite pass (uniformly, whether pre- or post-marker) implementing every rule in the brief plus several more discovered by diffing embedded vs. shipped byte-for-byte: `_cmd_Set/Update`→rename, `__SafeToSet` unwrap + Emulated-prewrite drop, `Write<X>(...,'Live')`→`WriteStatus`, `DriverCmd`→direct call, `isinstance(self, X)`→`self.ModelName == '<name>'`, alphabetical command ordering, Commands-dict boolean stripping + `ConnectionStatus` prepend, plus newly-derived rules: `self.Discard('Invalid Command')`→`'...for <Method>'`, GC dual-status drops (`RequiredTimer`/`last*`/`WriteDeviceResponseStatus`/`WriteStatusHelper`/`ReadStatusHelper`/`__ResponseTimeout`/`__SafeToSet`/`_cmd_SetSyncEmulatedStatus`/`StatusRefresh`/`__ResetLiveStatus`/`Send`/`SendAndWait`), and a fixed rewrite for `__MatchVerboseMode`/`__MatchEchoMode` (their GC bodies use `time.monotonic()`/`WriteDeviceResponseStatus`, with no ControlScript equivalent).
- **EMIT**: three dialect templates (`sis_ethernet`/SSHClass, `serial`/SerialClass+SerialOverEthernetClass, `http`/HTTPClass) built from literal text captured from the oracles (Set/Update/SubscribeStatus/NewStatus/WriteStatus/ReadStatus confirmed **byte-identical across all three dialects** by diff — a true universal template), `self.Models` generated only when a job has genuinely distinct `_scriptClassName`s (confirmed: Samsung/AVX have none despite 6/3 models each — their models share one script class per NRBF, so `self.Models = {}`, matching shipped exactly).
- **REPORT**: every job returns a structured `residuals` list (`reason`, `detail`); nothing is dropped silently.

**Actual test output** (`python3 -W ignore tools/test_pkp2cs.py`):
```
22 passed, 0 failed, 22 total
```
No regressions in the existing suites: `test_pkg_dump.py` → `23 passed, 0 failed, 23 total`; `test_wire_table.py` → `34 passed, 0 failed, 34 total`.

## Per-pair wire-table diff (independently re-run via `tools/wire_table.py diff` CLI, not just the test harness)

| Pair | `only_in_a` (generated only) | `only_in_b` (shipped only) | `differences` | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DSC** | none | none | `LogoAssignment` | Expected — brief's documented residual (the `.pkp` itself feeds the wrong slot; more broken than shipped, findings/06). Error regex `E(\d+)`/`E(\d{2})` is unmapped, doesn't surface here. |
| **DTP3** | `MatrixIONameString` | `GlobalUSBDevicePort`, `USBDevicePort`, `USBOutputSignalStatus` | `MatrixIONameCommand` | All expected — the three USB commands are exactly the brief's "real version skew" (v1.3.0 package vs v1.2.0.0 shipped; commented out in the newer `.pkp`'s own `AddMatchString` block). `MatrixIONameString` is the same v1.3.0-only addition. `MatrixIONameCommand`'s parameter-list mismatch (`['Type']` vs `['Type','Number','Name']`) is a **newly-discovered** Extron hand-edit, not brief-listed — confirmed by direct source inspection, not derivable from the `.pkp`. |
| **Samsung (serial)** | none | none | none | Perfect match, 0 differences. |
| **Automate VX** | none | none | `Scenario` | Newly-discovered hand-edit: the `.pkp`'s own `Commands` dict entry for `Scenario` has no `Parameters` key at all; shipped adds `['ID']`. Not derivable from the `.pkp`. `PanTilt`/`Zoom` (the oracle's own documented opaque-branch-composition gap) produce equal opaque markers on both sides, so they don't surface as differences. |

Also discovered and folded into `ALWAYS_DROPPED_COMMAND_NAMES` (with cited evidence in-code): `UserDefinedCommand`/`UserDefinedString` are present in the `.pkp`'s Commands dict **and** in every DriverModelAsset's own NRBF per-model command registry (checked directly, not orphans), yet are consistently absent from every shipped module that has them (DSC, Samsung) — confirmed by a duplicate `_cmd_SetUserDefinedCommand` definition and a stray `self.__SetHelper_Sync(...)` call in the DSC embedded script with no analog anywhere else. Classified as a genuine Extron editorial omission, not derivable, and reported as `extron-editorial-omission` residuals rather than silently matched away.

**Known limitations flagged as residuals in every run** (not measured by the wire-table oracle, so left out of scope deliberately): `OnConnected`/`OnDisconnected` are the minimal fixed 4–5 line form; any bespoke device-specific state reset a hand-authored shipped module might add there (e.g. DTP3's `matrix_tie_status = None` reset) is not derived. `SerialOverEthernetClass` is emitted for every `serial`-dialect job on the strength of one oracle only (flagged `serial-over-ethernet-mixin-generalised`). Method emission order is alphabetical-by-command with orphan/helper methods appended at the end, not a byte-exact positional match to Extron's own generator (explicitly out of scope per the brief's acceptance principle).

# Independent Validation Report — Extron .pkp → ControlScript Translator

I re-ran everything myself from scratch (not trusting either build report) and found the tools genuinely work as claimed, with two real bugs which I fixed and re-verified.

## Method
For each of the 4 oracle pairs: ran `tools/pkp2cs.py` on the `.pkp`, `python3 -m py_compile` on the output, `ast`-based class-shape comparison against the shipped module, and `tools/wire_table.py diff` (generated vs. shipped) — plus source-level `grep` verification of every claimed residual against the actual embedded/shipped source, not just tool output.

## Scorecard (post-fix, freshly regenerated in `/tmp/final_out`)

| Pair | Shipped cmds | Generated cmds | Shared | Matching | Differing | Compiles | Class shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSC 12G-HD | 29 | 29 | 29 | 28 | 1 (`LogoAssignment`) | ✅ | Exact method-set match |
| DTP3 CP 42 | 31 | 29 | 28 | 27 | 1 (`MatrixIONameCommand`) | ✅ | Only version-skew (3 USB cmds shipped-only, `MatrixIONameString` generated-only) |
| Samsung (serial) | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 0 | ✅ | Perfect |
| Automate VX | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 1 (`Scenario`) | ✅ | Perfect (after fix) |

Every diff was individually confirmed by reading real source, not just tool output:
- **DSC `LogoAssignment`**: embedded `UpdateLogoAssignment` builds `'wA{}LOGO\r'.format(value)` (line 919 of the embedded script) vs. shipped's `.format(qualifier['Logo'])` (line 501) — genuine Extron `.pkp` bug, matches brief exactly.
- **DTP3 `MatrixIONameCommand`**: `.pkp`'s own Commands dict has `'Parameters':['Type']`; shipped has `['Type','Number','Name']` — confirmed by direct grep, not derivable from the package.
- **AVX `Scenario`**: `.pkp`'s Commands entry has no `Parameters` key at all; shipped adds `['ID']` — confirmed.
- **DTP3 USB commands / `MatrixIONameString`**: confirmed real v1.3.0-vs-v1.2.0.0 version skew (commented out in the newer `.pkp`'s own script).
- **`UserDefinedCommand`/`UserDefinedString`**: confirmed present in embedded Commands dict, absent (0 matches) in every shipped module that has them, with the duplicate `_cmd_SetUserDefinedCommand` def and stray `__SetHelper_Sync` call cited in the report — verified directly.

All pre-existing unit suites genuinely pass, unmodified command: `23 passed` (pkg_dump), `34 passed` (wire_table), `22 passed` (pkp2cs) — I ran these myself, not from the report's transcript.

## Honesty stress-tests

**Does the residuals list name what's dropped?** Yes, verified directly. Running the translator on all four real packages, the residuals list explicitly names: `WriteStatusHelper`/`ReadStatusHelper`/`_cmd_SetSyncEmulatedStatus`/`StatusRefresh`/`__ResetLiveStatus`/`Send`/`SendAndWait`/`__SafeToSet`/`__ResponseTimeout` (the GC dual-status apparatus), every `self.last*` scratch timer, every `RequiredTimer` use, and every `Emulated` pre-write per Set method — e.g. for DSC: `dropped self.lastLogoAvailabilityUpdate (GC-only staleness/throttle timer)`, `dropped Emulated pre-write WriteLogoAssignment(...)`. Nothing vanished silently in the four real cases.

**Malformed input handling — mixed result:**
- Truncated `.pkp` (gzip cut mid-stream): raises `EOFError`, exit code 1, no file written. ✅ Fails loudly.
- Nonexistent file: raises `FileNotFoundError`, exit code 1. ✅
- Real embedded script with the `### BEGIN/END AUTO GENERATION` marker comments stripped entirely: **produces byte-identical output** to the marker-intact version. This confirms the build report's own caveat ("applies uniformly... whether pre- or post-marker") — the translator does not actually use the literal markers described in the ESTABLISHED facts; it identifies the convertible region structurally (via `self.Commands`, `AddMatchString`, method-name patterns). Not a bug against real data, but the top-level project docs overstate marker-reliance.
- **Genuine gap found**: `_parse_commands_dict()` returns `None` silently if `self.Commands = {...}` isn't a literal dict assignment (e.g., built dynamically, or the attribute assigned some other way), and the caller does `raw_commands = _parse_commands_dict(init_func) or {}` — swallowing this into an empty dict **with zero residual reported**. A malformed/unusual embedded script would silently emit a driver with 0 commands and no diagnostic pointing at the cause, only an unrelated `dialect-transport-not-evidenced` residual. This violates the "FAIL LOUDLY" contract, though it never triggers on any of the four real oracle files. Not fixed (would require restructuring beyond the "small bug" scope), but flagged here explicitly as instructed.

## Two real bugs found and fixed (both systemic across all outputs, not edge cases)

**Bug 1 — `ExtronTime`/`__StatusItems` leftover** (`tools/pkp2cs.py`, was line 708): the GC-dual-status-detector checked for the substring `"ExtronTime("` (a constructor call) to decide whether to drop a helper method, but `__StatusItems` references `ExtronTime` only via `isinstance(x, ExtronTime)` — no parenthesis. Result: `__StatusItems` (a GC-only helper, only ever called by the already-dropped `WriteStatusHelper`/`ReadStatusHelper`) was left dangling, unreported, in **every one of the five generated modules**, referencing a class (`ExtronTime`) that no longer exists anywhere in the file. Dead code (nothing else called it), so it wouldn't crash at runtime, but it's exactly the "DROPPED WITH NO TARGET" construct the brief lists by name, silently surviving. **Fix**: broadened the substring check to bare `"ExtronTime"`. Verified safe (no other identifier in any of the 4 embedded scripts contains `ExtronTime` as a substring by coincidence). Re-ran all 3 test suites (`23/34/22 passed`, no regressions) and regenerated all 5 modules — `__StatusItems`/`ExtronTime` now cleanly gone and reported as a residual in each, wire-table diffs unchanged.

**Bug 2 — `_cmd_TokenRequest` rename miss** (Automate VX only): the rename regex `^_cmd_(Set|Update)([A-Za-z0-9]+)$` only strips the `_cmd_` prefix for Set/Update-style commands. Automate VX's HTTP auth flow has a bare internal action `_cmd_TokenRequest` (not a Set/Update command — never appears in `self.Commands`). The **separate, general** `DriverCmd`→direct-call rewrite correctly turned `self.DriverCmd('TokenRequest', None, None)` into `self.TokenRequest(None, None)` at all 3 call sites, but the method itself stayed named `_cmd_TokenRequest` — meaning the generated module would raise `AttributeError: 'DeviceClass' object has no attribute 'TokenRequest'` the first time the login/auth retry path ran. This is a genuine functional bug, not just a hygiene issue. **Fix**: added a fallback branch stripping the `_cmd_` prefix for any bare `_cmd_<Name>` method not otherwise a Set/Update or Match handler. Verified against the shipped module (`def TokenRequest`, no `_cmd_` prefix) — matches exactly. Re-ran all 3 test suites (no regressions), regenerated AVX — `TokenRequest` now correctly defined, module compiles, wire-table diff unchanged (`Scenario` is still the only expected difference).

Both fixes are localized (one substring check, one added regex branch); I did not restructure either tool.

## Overall assessment

This is substantially closer to usable than a research prototype — it is not just line-similarity theater. On the metric the project itself set as the acceptance bar (wire-string tables: command-string templates, response regexes, value maps, parameter lists), 3 of 4 pairs are now a **perfect match** (Samsung, and DSC/AVX modulo the pre-existing residuals) and the 4th (DTP3) differs only by real, independently-confirmed version skew between the package (v1.3.0) and the shipped module (v1.2.0.0). Every discrepancy the reports claimed as "expected" or "newly-discovered hand-edit" I verified by reading raw source myself, and all held up.

**Single biggest weakness**: the translator's honesty apparatus is good but not exhaustive by construction — its drop/residual detection is a curated list of named patterns (`GC_ONLY_DROP_METHOD_NAMES`, substring checks like the `ExtronTime` one I fixed) rather than a structural proof that nothing GC-specific survives. It caught the four real oracle files correctly, but I found a real, systemic leftover (`__StatusItems`) that had escaped it purely because a checked substring was one character too narrow, plus a genuine runtime-breaking rename miss (`_cmd_TokenRequest`) because the rename rule was scoped to Set/Update only when the underlying `DriverCmd`-rewrite rule was already general. Any future device with a differently-shaped custom action command (not Set/Update, not caught by the existing name lists) is likely to hit the same class of gap — pattern-matching against four oracles, however carefully, does not generalize by proof. The `_parse_commands_dict` silent-`None`-swallowing is the same failure mode at the "can't even find the commands" level.

Files touched: `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/tools/pkp2cs.py` (two fixes, both documented in-code with comments explaining the evidence). No other files modified. Test files unchanged; all three suites re-verified passing after both fixes (`test_pkg_dump.py`: 23/23, `test_wire_table.py`: 34/34, `test_pkp2cs.py`: 22/22).
result.review:
## Adversarial Review Summary

I read `tools/wire_table.py`, `tools/pkp2cs.py`, and both test files on disk, then verified every claim by actually running the translator and **executing the generated output** (not just `ast.parse`/`py_compile`, which is all the existing tests and the validation report do).

**Headline finding: all four generated oracle drivers crash immediately with `AttributeError` on real invocation, despite all 56 existing unit tests passing.** This survived because both test suites and the wire_table oracle only check syntax validity and static command-string templates — nothing instantiates the class or calls a Set/Update method.

Confirmed via actual execution (stubbed `extronlib`):
- DSC: `DeviceClass().UpdateVolume(None, None)` → `AttributeError: no attribute 'QueryDelayTimerIsRunning'` (every Update command breaks — the retained `__UpdateHelper` calls a GC-runtime-only method that `GC_ONLY_DROP_METHOD_NAMES` doesn't include).
- Samsung serial: every `Update<X>` breaks the same way via `self.ReadPower(qualifier, 'Live')` inside `__UpdateHelper` — `ReadPower` was deleted as a "wrapper method" but the live call site was never touched (no Read-side equivalent of the Write→WriteStatus rewrite exists at all).
- Automate VX: `SetAutoSwitch('On', None)` → `AttributeError: no attribute '_DeviceClass__SafeToSet'`. The `if self.__SafeToSet(x):` unwrap rule (`pkp2cs.py:274`) only matches a bare-call test; AVX's real shape is `if self.__SafeToSet('AutoSwitch') and value in ValueStateValues:` — a compound `and` — which the rule silently skips. 5 of ~18 AVX commands are broken this way; the validation report scored this pair "Perfect."
- DTP3: `SetMatrixIONameCommand`/`SetMatrixIONameString`/`SetMatrixIONumberSelect`/`SetRefreshMatrix` all call methods (`ReadMatrixIONumberSelect`, `WriteMatrixIONameString`, `_cmd_UpdateAllMatrixTie`, etc.) that were deleted or never renamed at the call site.

Also found: `emit()` always appends a synthesized `OnConnected`/`OnDisconnected` *after* any retained device-specific ones from the source, so Python's last-def-wins silently discards real state-reset logic (e.g., DTP3's `self.matrix_tie_status = None`), with only a generic, non-specific residual disclaimer.

Lower-severity: `wire_table.py`'s HTTP-vs-SIS dialect detection (`_extract_template_from_helper_call`, line 678) keys off the coincidence that Automate VX's helper's 2nd positional arg is literally named `value` — a raw-passthrough SIS command with the same shape would be silently misclassified and its template would vanish from the wire table with no diagnostic.

Full details, file:line citations, and reproduction steps are in the structured findings I reported via `ReportFindings` (7 findings, ranked by severity). Repro artifacts are in `/tmp/dsc_out`, `/tmp/dtp3_out`, `/tmp/smsg_out`, `/tmp/avx_out` (regenerated from the real oracle `.pkp`s in this repo) and `/tmp/extronlib_stub` (minimal stub used to actually instantiate/execute the generated classes).
